The Senior Manager, GTS Digital Enablement serves as the centralized leader responsible for driving data and digital governance execution, data stewardship, lifecycle management, and operational readiness across the GTS business digital portfolio. Role Overview

As a Principal Data Scientist within Coupang’s Supply Chain Management Autonomation (SCMA) organization, you will serve as the scientific authority and primary architect for our Cognitive Engine. You will be the bridge between cutting-edge Deep Learning (signal sensing) and Operations Research (constraint-based optimization).

Your mission is to transform Coupang’s supply chain into a durable competitive advantage by building a fully autonomous, agentic operating system that is capable of multi-step reasoning, where LLMs interpret signals and OR models execute procurement decisions without manual intervention. This system will manage procurement decisions for 10M+ units daily, with the goal of reducing manual execution by 50% while maximizing inventory ROI and in-stock rates.

Key Responsibilities

• Architect the Cognitive Engine: Lead the synthesis of Large Language Models (LLMs), Knowledge Graphs (KGs), and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to create an autonomous, agentic supply chain platform.
• Integrate DL & OR: Design hybrid systems that utilize Deep Learning for high-fidelity signal sensing and Operations Research for complex, constraint-based optimization.
• Drive Full Autonomy: Develop models that proactively manage the entire SKU lifecycle at hyper-scale, moving from "human-in-the-loop" to "human-on-the-loop" strategic oversight.
• Establish Model Governance: Implement strict governance frameworks to ensure high-stakes autonomous decisions remain accurate, unbiased, explainable, and resilient to data drift.
• Simulate & Experiment: Lead Large-scale Discrete Event Simulations (DES) and Agent-Based Simulation models to validate "what-if" scenarios before production deployment.
• Strategic Leadership: Advise leadership on the research roadmap and technical breakthroughs that will define the future of e-commerce supply chain management .
• Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner with SCMA Engineering to deploy production-grade models that handle extreme demand volatility without compromising latency or reliability.

Qualifications & Technical Requirements

• Education: Ph.D. or Master’s in Operations Research, Computer Science (AI/ML focus), or a related quantitative field.
• Experience: 10+ years of relevant industry experience, ideally in e-commerce, SCM, or high-complexity trading environments.
• AI/ML Expertise: Hands-on experience designing and implementing:

• Model Architectures: Experience with state-of-the-art time-series and graph architectures (e.g., TiDE, GNNs, Transformers), and experiences in Reinforcement learning models.
• Generative AI: Expert-level knowledge of LLMs and Agentic workflows.
• Graphs: Knowledge Graphs and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for supply chain mapping.

• Optimization & Heuristics: Deep proficiency in Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP), Dynamic Programming, and Meta-heuristics (Genetic Algorithms, PSO).
• Simulation Mastery: Proven track record in Discrete Event Simulation or Agent-Based modeling (e.g., AnyLogic, Simio).
• Tooling:

• Solvers: Expertise in Gurobi, Cplex, or SCIP.
• Languages: Python, Java, or Scala.
• Data: SQL mastery and experience with Big Data environments (Spark, Clickhouse).

WHAT YOU'LL DO

We're looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer for Midjourney Medical — from precision electromechanical assemblies up to the large-scale structures and mechanisms that hold everything together and make it move. This role spans the full range of scale: one week you might be refining a compact transducer mount, the next you're architecting a structural frame or designing the motion system that positions hardware within it.

This is a hands-on role on a small cross-functional team. You'll take problems from whiteboard sketch to working hardware yourself — designing in CAD, prototyping in the shop, testing, iterating, and integrating with research teams, electrical and software engineers along the way. We move fast and expect you to drive your own work: identifying what needs to happen next, making sound engineering calls without waiting for permission, and shipping hardware that works.

- Own parts of the mechanical systems end to end — structures, mechanisms, and electromechanical integration

- Design large-scale structures: frames, weldments, enclosures, and support systems, with attention to stiffness, weight, manufacturability, and serviceability

- Design mechanisms: linkages, motion stages, actuation systems for precise, reliable positioning and articulation

- Integrate transducers, electronics, cabling, and thermal management into large physical systems

- Perform engineering analysis (tolerance stack-ups, structural/FEA, mechanism kinematics) to de-risk designs before committing to hardware

- Build and test relentlessly — 3D printing, rapid prototyping, and hands-on fabrication are core to how you'll validate designs

- Select parts and materials for system-level integration, balancing performance, cost, and lead time

- Drive projects independently from concept through validation, and collaborate closely with a small cross-disciplinary team to hit project goals

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field

- 5+ years of experience designing and shipping electromechanical hardware

- Demonstrated track record in mechanism design — you can point to mechanisms you've designed that work reliably in the real world

- Experience designing larger-scale structures (frames, gantries, enclosures, or similar), not just component-level parts

- Proficiency in CAD (we use OnShape) for design, optimization, and system integration

- Strong rapid-prototyping experience — this is a must; you should be as comfortable in the shop as at your desk

- Background in R&D environments where the problem isn't fully defined and the path forward is yours to figure out

- Excellent creative problem-solving and analytical skills

- Experience working closely with a small cross-disciplinary team

jobs.description: Are you passionate about large power infrastructure systems? Do you love to innovate, discover, and apply your knowledge to advance world-class systems? We are looking for candidates with proven ability to influence technical teams, a track record of delivering complex products from design and specification through deployment, and a deep understanding of power generation designs. At Amazon Web Services (AWS), our data centers are industry leading examples of innovation in the areas of data center critical infrastructure design, space utilization, energy efficiency, and cost effectiveness. We are known for our speed to market, reliability, and lowest total cost of ownership. Our engineers are on the forefront of creating and delivering the most innovative products to our customers and are known for being a diverse and upbeat team that is continually improving the world of cloud computing. AWS’s work environment is unique and offers an exceptional opportunity for the right candidate. As a Senior Product Engineer, Power Generation, you will serve as the Subject Matter Expert and technical leader within the Power Generation Solutions team for the evaluation, development, design, and deployment of primary, temporary, and backup power products and equipment. You will own complex and ambiguous problems that span multiple teams and drive technical decisions that impact AWS’ global infrastructure strategy. You will lead developing different power and energy equipment to exceed our customer’s expectations for delivering power to our data centers. You will seek new ways to enhance the reliability, scalability, and cost effectiveness of our engineering products and designs. You will have the ability to drive change and make a substantial impact in the systems our customers rely on. Additionally, you will have a key role in defining, modifying, evaluating, and validating product designs against AWS’ strict requirements for safety, availability, cost, and sustainability impacts. This may include equipment selection and sizing, product design development, engineering drawings and diagrams, specifications, and participate in project development. Your technical expertise on will guide cross-functional teams in making critical design decisions, evaluating trade-offs, integrating new technologies, and managing technical risks across complex power systems. Amazon has a global presence, therefore, domestic and international travel may be necessary. Teamwork is absolutely necessary for us to accomplish our goals. You must be able to work within a team and collaborate with others to accomplish the required tasks. This includes working with internal groups as well as external suppliers and consultants, including utilities, manufacturers, vendors, and contractors. About the team The Power Generation Solutions team creates and delivers product and engineering solutions in for power and energy to help advance AWS’ mission to deliver world-leading cloud services. Our solutions are guided by four main principles; unlocking capacity growth, maintaining high infrastructure uptime, minimizing infrastructure costs, and advancing our net-zero carbon Climate Pledge. To deliver these solutions, our team provides technical input to realize a shared vision and strategy with partner teams and provides engineering support across the project or product lifecycle to deliver the solution. We also provide grid analytics and manage and develop models for determining the total energy and water use within our fleet of data centers and work with partners on improving overall performance.

The Instrumentation Controls and Electrical (ICE) Supervisor is responsible for leading and coordinating Instrumentation, Controls, and Electrical maintenance activities across production and water facilities. This position oversees ICE technicians, corrective and preventative maintenance, routine calibrations, safety shutdown systems, equipment reliability, training, and work scheduling through Maximo.

The role works closely with Operations, Water, Production Control Center, Completions, Internal Gas Measurement, SCADA, Automation, Engineering, and other support groups to ensure facilities are maintained safely, reliably, and efficiently throughout their operating lifecycle.

The Instrumentation Controls and Electrical (ICE) Supervisor responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Leadership

• Coordinate and prioritize corrective maintenance activities with ICE technicians.
• Support troubleshooting of instrumentation, electrical, controls, communications, measurement, and safety systems.
• Manage emergency and high-priority maintenance response.
• Identify recurring failures and drive long-term corrective actions.
• Ensure maintenance activities are completed safely, efficiently, and properly documented.

Planning and Scheduling

• Schedule and manage technician work through Maximo.
• Prioritize work based on safety, production impact, equipment criticality, and operational needs.
• Maintain visibility of open work orders, backlog, overdue work, and completion status.
• Coordinate maintenance around outages, completions activity, facility startups, and operational priorities.

Preventative Maintenance and Calibration

• Establish, maintain, and continuously improve the ICE preventative maintenance program.
• Ensure routine instrumentation calibrations are completed at required frequencies.
• Maintain PM and calibration requirements for critical production and water facility equipment.
• Monitor PM compliance and correct overdue or ineffective maintenance activities.
• Use equipment history and failure trends to improve maintenance strategies.

Safety Systems

• Oversee inspection, testing, calibration, and maintenance of facility safety and shutdown systems.
• Ensure transmitters, switches, alarms, trips, interlocks, and emergency shutdown devices are maintained and tested.
• Coordinate safety system testing with Operations, PCC, SCADA, and other affected groups.
• Ensure deficiencies in critical protective systems are corrected promptly.

Production and Water Facility Support

• Oversee ICE maintenance for production gas and water facilities.
• Support instrumentation, electrical, controls, communications, measurement, pumps, tanks, and associated field equipment.
• Coordinate with Water, Completions, Internal Gas Measurement, SCADA, and Operations.
• Support facility commissioning, startup, shutdown, outage, reactivation, and transition into long-term operations.

Electrical Safety and NFPA 70E

• Oversee ICE electrical maintenance activities up to and including 480 VAC within the approved scope of the department.
• Ensure technicians are trained, qualified, and authorized for the electrical work they perform.
• Ensure ICE technicians maintain required NFPA 70E training and qualifications.
• Coordinate initial and refresher electrical safety training as required.
• Reinforce safe electrical work practices, including lockout/tagout, absence-of-voltage verification, proper PPE, approach boundaries, and arc-flash requirements.
• Maintain awareness of technician qualifications and ensure personnel work within their authorized level of training.

Equipment Lifecycle Management

• Maintain ICE equipment standards throughout the lifecycle of production and water facilities.
• Ensure equipment is properly documented in Maximo with asset records, specifications, PM requirements, calibration frequencies, and maintenance history.
• Identify obsolete, unreliable, or unsupported equipment and coordinate replacement.
• Provide maintenance input during equipment selection, construction, commissioning, and facility modifications.
• Work with Automation, Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain to improve equipment standardization.

Technician Leadership and Development

• Provide direct leadership, coaching, and technical support to ICE technicians.
• Establish training plans based on equipment, safety requirements, technology, and identified skill gaps.
• Coordinate vendor and manufacturer training where needed.
• Develop technician capabilities in instrumentation, electrical, controls, SCADA, communications, measurement, calibration, and troubleshooting.
• Promote accountability, consistent work practices, and strong equipment ownership.

Reliability and Continuous Improvement

• Review equipment failures and maintenance history to identify reliability improvements.
• Support root cause investigations and corrective actions for significant or repeat failures.
• Track key maintenance metrics including PM compliance, calibration compliance, backlog, repeat failures, emergency work, and equipment reliability.
• Identify opportunities to reduce downtime, repeat work, and operating cost.

Required Experience and Skills

• High school diploma or equivalent.
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in instrumentation, electrical, controls, automation, industrial maintenance, oil and gas operations, or a related technical field.
• Experience troubleshooting and maintaining industrial instrumentation and electrical equipment.
• Working knowledge of electrical systems up to 480 VAC.
• Knowledge of preventative maintenance, calibration, and safety shutdown systems.
• Familiarity with NFPA 70E and electrical safe work practices.
• Experience with Maximo or a similar maintenance management system.
• Strong leadership, planning, scheduling, communication, and organizational skills.
• Ability to read electrical drawings, P&IDs, control drawings, and technical documentation.

Preferred Experience and Skills

• Associate or bachelor's degree in Electrical Technology, Instrumentation, Automation, Electronics, Engineering Technology, Industrial Maintenance, or a related field.

• Oil and gas production or water facility maintenance experience.
• Experience with PLCs, RTUs, SCADA, industrial communications, gas measurement, transmitters, control valves, and electrical distribution.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

•

Handles all assigned claims promptly and effectively, with little direction and oversight, which may include complicated and catastrophic losses. Makes decisions within delegated authority, recommends settlement values in the disposition of claims as outlined in company policies and procedures.

Accurately pays claims based on policy provisions, state mandates and/or fee schedules.

Initiates and conducts follow-ups through proficient use of the claims and other related business systems.

Education: Undergraduate degree or equivalent experience preferred. Advanced degrees in law or related field desirable.

License/Certification/Designation: Successful completion of required claims certification schools or courses. Professional development such as IIA or CPCU preferred. State licensing where required. Obtain Xactimate Level 1 certification within a year of start date. Obtain Xactimate Level 2 certification within two years of employment.

Experience: Five years of experience handling property claims, insurance processing or field claims adjusting.

Knowledge, Abilities and Skills: General knowledge of insurance theory and practices, and contracts and their application. Property estimating and automated claims systems. Ability to establish repair requirements and cost estimates for property losses. Ability to evaluate and successfully advise on property claims. Organizational skills to prioritize work. Command of written and verbal communication skills to effectively communicate with policyholders, claimants, repairpersons, attorneys, agents and the general public. Must be willing to work irregular hours and to travel with possible overnight requirements. May be on-call. Must be available to work catastrophes (CAT). Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Sales Lead, Canada Public Sector at Anthropic, you'll drive the adoption of safe, frontier AI across the Canadian public sector. You'll leverage your deep understanding of Canadian government operations and consultative sales expertise to propel revenue growth while becoming a trusted partner to customers, helping them embed and deploy AI while uncovering its full range of capabilities. In collaboration with GTM, product, and marketing teams, you'll help refine our approach to the Canadian public-sector market while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance. This is a national role anchored in the National Capital Region, supporting the Government of Canada, provincial/territorial governments, Canada's national security and defence community, crown corporations, and the broader public sector.

• Drive new business and revenue growth across the Canadian public sector, with the Government of Canada as the primary focus and provincial/territorial governments, crown corporations, and the broader public sector as secondary coverage, owning the full sales cycle from initial outreach through deployment

• Build and maintain relationships with key decision-makers across the Government of Canada, including departmental Chief Information Officers and Chief Data Officers, senior program executives, central agency and procurement stakeholders, and mission owners, becoming a trusted advisor on AI capabilities and implementation
• Develop and execute strategic account plans that align with departmental mandates and modernization initiatives, positioning Anthropic early in major programs to shape requirements before they are finalized
• Navigate Canadian security and compliance requirements, including data classification levels, federal security control profiles, assessment and authorization, data-residency requirements, and personnel security clearances
• Coordinate closely with cloud service providers and system integrators to ensure successful deployment and integration
• Represent Anthropic at Canadian public-sector and partner events, including industry days, conferences, and cloud provider events, raising Anthropic's profile through speaking engagements and community engagement
• Provide detailed market intelligence and customer feedback to product teams to ensure our offerings meet Canadian public-sector requirements, including responsible-AI obligations under the Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making and the Algorithmic Impact Assessment
• Create and maintain sales playbooks specific to Canadian public-sector use cases and procurement processes
• Generate pipeline and own territory and account planning across your assigned Canadian public-sector accounts, maintaining hands-on engagement with key accounts
• Collaborate across teams to ensure coordinated delivery of commitments and maintain appropriate documentation of customer engagements, engaging bilingually (English/French) with federal institutions and Quebec public-sector customers where required

You may be a good fit if you have:

• 7+ years of enterprise sales experience in the Canadian public sector, the majority selling to the Government of Canada, with a proven track record of driving adoption of emerging technologies
• Deep understanding of federal department and agency mandates, challenges, and technology needs, with working knowledge of provincial/territorial and broader public-sector buyers
• Demonstrated ability to balance strategic account leadership with hands-on sales execution
• Familiarity with how the Government of Canada buys and secures cloud and AI services, with the judgment to navigate these processes alongside partners, capture, and deal teams
• Strong track record of exceeding revenue targets and closing large, complex, long-cycle public-sector deals
• Ability to be based in the National Capital Region, with travel across Canada as needed
• Eligibility to obtain and maintain a Government of Canada personnel security clearance (Reliability Status; Secret an asset)
• Executive presence and relationship-building skills across all levels, from technical teams to senior agency leadership (ADM/DG)
• Proven ability to coordinate across multiple stakeholders, including cloud providers and system integrators
• Professional working proficiency in French, sufficient to support Quebec public-sector engagement and bilingual delivery of customer-facing material
• Strategic thinking combined with attention to detail in execution
• A passion for safe and ethical AI development, with the ability to articulate its importance in government contexts

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$420,000—$495,000 CAD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.description: Why Join GEICO? At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities. Reports To: Senior Director, Marketing Transformation & Operations Job Description At GEICO, we offer a rewarding career where your ambitions are met with endless possibilities. Every day we honor our iconic brand by offering quality coverage to millions of customers and being there when they need us most. We thrive through relentless innovation to exceed our customers’ expectations while making a real impact for our company through our shared purpose. Role Purpose The Director, Marketing Ventures is the builder who makes GEICO Marketing’s capability strategy real. GEICO Marketing has laid out an ambitious plan for the capabilities it needs to own, build, and modernize — this role’s job is to stand them up: launching new capabilities from scratch, bringing in-housing to life, and building the agency and partner relationships that support everything the venture builds. This is an incubation role, not a planning role. We’re looking for someone who has personally built or scaled new groups before, ideally in modern, fast-moving disciplines that sit at the edge of content, culture, and audience — the kind of work most marketing organizations haven’t yet figured out how to structure. The same incubation mindset extends back into GEICO’s existing capabilities: constantly assessing what’s working, what needs a refresh, and where the operating model has to evolve. We view our capabilities not only in house, but also as hybrid and outsourced models. As such, this role also owns the agency and partner ecosystem end-to-end from sourcing and onboarding through day-to-day management, performance measurement, and governance — so that every partner relationship runs like a well-managed extension of the marketing organization. Sitting at the intersection of strategy, incubation, and execution, this role partners closely with capability owners across Marketing, Supply Management, and agency partners. Key Responsibilities Capability Incubation & Build Take GEICO Marketing’s capability strategy and make it real: launch new capabilities end-to-end, from pilot through scaled, steady-state operation. Personally build the first version of a new capability when needed — the team, the workflow, the tools — rather than only designing it on paper. Lead the in-housing of capabilities currently run externally, managing the transition of talent, process, and knowledge without disrupting delivery. Diagnose what a fragile or underperforming new capability needs and re-architect it across talent, process, technology, and operating model. Bring an incubation mindset to everything: treat every capability, new or existing, as something to keep testing, refining, and improving rather than something to set and leave. Manage third-party consultants and embedded partners supporting incubation efforts. Elevating Existing Capabilities Partner with existing capability owners to raise the bar on capabilities GEICO already runs, applying the same rigor used to stand up new ones. Identify capabilities that are stalled, under-resourced, or falling behind modern practice, and bring an incubation approach to help them catch up. Ensure capabilities that graduate from incubation continue to have a place to go for support, refresh, and reinvention as the market moves. Agency & Partner Management Own GEICO’s agency and partner operating model, defining clear roles, decision rights, and ways of working across internal teams and external partners. Build and maintain the agency scorecard program — defining KPIs, performance thresholds, and scoring methodology across every agency of record and key specialized partner. Own the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) process for major agency relationships: setting the agenda, consolidating performance data, facilitating sessions with capability owners and agency leadership, and driving accountability on action items. Partner closely with Supply Management on sourcing new capabilities and partners — co-leading market scans, RFI/RFP strategy, and vendor evaluation to ensure sourcing is competitive, compliant, and aligned to enterprise sourcing standards. Partner with Supply Management and Legal on agency negotiations, renewals, and contract terms, ensuring commercial and performance terms reinforce the operating model. Lead RFIs/RFPs and onboarding for new agencies and specialized partners, ensuring alignment to capability needs, cultural fit, and modern working practices. Resolve performance issues quickly through structured corrective action plans, in partnership with capability owners and Supply Management, driving continuous improvement and cost-saving initiatives. Serve as the primary point of integration between agencies, consultants, and internal capability owners, ensuring partners feel like a true extension of the GEICO marketing organization. AI & Modern Tools Enablement Partner closely with Marketing Technology and AI leaders to embed AI, automation, and advanced analytics as force multipliers within every capability this role builds or elevates. Champion AI and modern tools based on demonstrated business value, usability, and scalability. Actively stay ahead of AI and marketing technology trends and translate them into practical opportunities for capability advancement. Has personally built or incubated a marketing capability before — stood up the team, shipped the first version, and learned what broke along the way. Deep agency relationships: has operated on both sides of the agency-client table and knows how to structure a partnership that works for both. Comfortable in modern, fast-moving marketing disciplines that don’t have an established playbook yet. Applies the same builder energy to improving what already exists, not only to what’s new. Resilient and adaptable: thrives in ambiguity and keeps momentum through change. Qualifications 10+ years of experience building, launching, or scaling marketing capabilities inside agencies, incubators, or in-house teams — with a track record of capabilities you personally developed. Deep, established relationships across agency and partner networks, with experience on both sides of the relationship. Direct experience in and around modern, fast-evolving marketing disciplines that sit at the edge of content, culture, and audience. jobs.description: AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. As part of the AWS Controls Team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for innovating, deploying, optimizing, and maintaining the automation systems within the data centers. Automation systems consist of building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. The ideal candidate will possess a construction management, mechanical, electrical or technology background that enables them to undertake the challenges of sophisticated controls platforms and a demonstrated ability to think broadly and strategically in aligning building controls and automation with the larger objectives of the business. This role requires valid driver’s license and travel domestically and internationally at least 25% of the time. Key job responsibilities • Manage scope of Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) for construction of AWS data centers. • Ensure data center controls are deployed in accordance with scope of work (SOW) and specifications. • Review and provide feedback on mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) drawings. • Develop controls bill of material (BOM). • Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate difficult situations. • Work under tight project timelines. • Financially manage both construction and service contracts. • Act in a project sponsor/lead capacity. • Provide vendor management. • Develop scope of work for site improvement projects. • Provide technical assistance and support to internal customers during life cycle of the data center. • Perform controls root cause analysis for service of controls for AWS data centers. • Schedule and supervise Quarterly maintenance for BMS and EPMS. • Review controls sequence of operation and provide feedback to design. • Participate in a global on-call schedule. • Grow in technical ability by learning a multitude of different automation platforms. • Develop building automation controls drawings and wiring diagrams. • Size controls valves and damper actuators and select controls devices. • Develop and modify control logic programming. • Develop and modify graphical user interface.
